To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
context-aware pervasive learning environments have been used in many different ways in various educational settings and the use of mobile devices is increasing.

(a) the most commonly used technologies are RFID and Wi-Fi, (b) the learning models used in the reviewed systems are mostly not validated, (c) client-server architectures and mobile devices are used most commonly, (d) most of the reviewed systems support multiple simultaneous users and virtual communication, and (e) physical environments in pervasive environments are used mostly as contexts for learning and system resources.
(i) the reviewed systems were mostly based on client-server architectures; (ii) RFID was the common sensor technology; and (iii) mobile devices were the most common means of representing information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the common features of the reviewed papers, and with suggesting future research directions.
the role of context-aware pervasive learning environments in education and the potential benefits that they can provide.
the design of a pervasive learning environment that supports multiple users in a collaborative learning situation, and that is able to support the learning of multiple subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lack of evidence for the use of pervasive learning systems.
there is no clear evidence of the effectiveness of context-aware pervasive learning environments, and that there is a lack of research in the area.
the current state-of-the-art of context-aware pervasive learning systems is in its infancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to investigate the role of mobile technologies in learning and to develop suitable learning models for pervasive learning environments.
context-aware pervasive learning environments should be developed based on validated learning models, and that mobile devices could be more actively used in these environments.
the reviewed systems are mostly prototypes that are not yet ready for deployment in real-world learning environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a comprehensive framework to support the development of context-aware pervasive learning environments.
the current state of the art of context-aware pervasive learning environments is still immature.
the reviewed systems were not designed to be used in the real-world.
